subject: strandbeest
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: wind-walking beach creature of tubes.
Style: Theo Jansen kinetic sculpture.
reasoning:
I'm envisioning a Strandbeest-style beach creature built from tubes and rods, with a spine frame, cloth sails on top, and Jansen-linkage legs — keeping the rig simple with a root body joint plus leg joints to drive the walking motion.

Setting dimensions around 3m long and 1.8m tall with multiple leg pairs along the body, I'm working through the Jansen linkage geometry: crank pins, pivots, and the classic Holy numbers ratios that define the leg's rod lengths for realistic walking motion.

Working out circle-intersection math for each linkage joint...

Still working out the Jansen linkage dimensions, building in a fallback so intersection failures don't break the geometry, since I'm relying on approximated standard lengths for the rods.

This is getting too tangled with exact distances, so I'll simplify: compute circle intersections for each joint with a fallback for degenerate cases, then just normalize the whole model vertically at the end by finding the lowest foot position and shifting everything so it rests at ground level.

For the leg layout, I'm placing twelve legs total in phase-offset pairs along the body's length, each pair sitting in its own x-plane with a shared crank phase driving the walking motion.

For each leg I'm sketching out the full linkage chain -- the frame link, the connecting rods, the crank rod, and joint spheres at the key pivot points -- plus a small foot cap, so each leg ends up as a cluster of parts repeated across all twelve.

Then I'm turning to the body frame itself: a truss of longerons running top and bottom, positioned relative to the pivot shaft height, with the leg mounting planes set outboard of the bottom rails, and zigzag diagonal rods and cross ribs tying the top and bottom rails together into a rigid skeleton.

Now for the mechanism and decoration, I'm adding central axle rods along each side of the shaft at x=±0.4, then designing "sails" as Jansen-style bottle wind-catchers — rows of capsule-shaped translucent forms racked along a top spine like wings, standing in for the strandbeest's characteristic bottle sails.

Mapping out two rows of 16 angled capsule bottles each, rising wing-like from the spine, with small cap cylinders on top and alternating pale colors. I'm also considering support ribs, a front mast with a wind vane and tail, and small front details like sensor-eyes to give the creature a face.

Now I'm sketching the rear ballast tanks as blue cylinders hung under the body, then planning a helper function for rods and a single root joint placement that depends on computing leg height first. I'm defining a leg-point function that maps angles into 3D coordinates with a scale factor, working out the right proportions so the legs aren't too tall relative to the body.

Writing leg phase and intersection math...

I'm trying to pin down the sign convention for each intersection point in the linkage, reasoning through which side of the line each joint (D, E, F) should fall on based on the Jansen mechanism's geometry, then plan to compute the foot point from there.

Good enough as a fallback with finite results. Now I'm setting up the color palette for the parts—lemon-yellow tubes, joint spheres, steel fittings, bottles, caps, and sand—then precomputing the leg geometry across both symmetric sides.

For each leg set I'm placing a primary and secondary parallel rod with phase offsets following the Jansen linkage pattern, giving roughly 24 legs with ~13 parts each, totaling around 400 parts, comfortably under budget. I'm writing a rod helper function that generates 3D points between two endpoints with configurable radius, color, and polygon detail for the cross-section.
